mw drive send open --to MEMBER [--id SLUG] GOAL...
mw drive send task|steer|note ID N TEXT...   (note N: 0 = the drive itself)
mw drive send result ID N pass|fail [TEXT...]   (remote)
mw drive send stop|close ID   (driver) | mw drive send pause ID   (remote)
mw drive recv [LINE]   (no LINE: read it from stdin, e.g. a quoted heredoc)
mw drive resume ID
mw drive status [-j]
mw drive check --idle DUR [--at RFC3339] [-j]
Records a session-to-session drive on both boards; mw sends nothing (the line travels over SendMessage).
Wire line: mw-drive ID SEQ EVENT [N] [TEXT], ASCII, TEXT at most 400 characters without [ or ]. The open line is
mw-drive ID 1 open MEMBER GOAL (MEMBER = the remote tenant). ID is MEMBER.SLUG (at most 30 characters from a-z 0-9 . -),
the ticket is drive.ID. SEQ counts per sender and drive: at or below the last applied one prints dup, a gap is DRIVE_STATE.
Options come before the event, the id or the goal; everything after ID N (or after the goal starts) is literal TEXT.
Every drive command needs a registered, running named session (-s NAME or MW_SESSION); a tenant with a tracker refuses drive.
One drive per session as remote (a second open prints a busy line, also when the session is driving); a driven session cannot drive.
result N pass needs task N already done with mw done on the remote's board; the driver's mirror closes as no-evidence.
check lists only the remote drives held by the calling session.
recv prints the reply line when there is one (busy, closed, dup), exit 0. A malformed line exits 1 (USAGE); an event that does not
fit the drive's state exits 2 (DRIVE_STATE). TEXT is stored only in notes labelled [data from MEMBER], never in titles.
See USAGE.md, "Drive".

Common names when shown: -t/--tenant, -s/--session, -j/--json, -v/--verbose.
Run `mw help` for all commands and flag mappings.
